purpose: Question bank for MUC-5 experiments that are small enough for the cloudtainer but interesting enough to shape later ML work.

questions.question: When the construction space is enumerable, which methods find strong deck+mulligan+pilot bundles fastest: enumeration, evolutionary search, neural policy search, PSRO-style response generation, or hybrids?
questions.why_it_matters: Enumeration gives a truth-ish baseline for deck vectors, but not for pilots. Learned/evolved methods must justify themselves by sample efficiency, robustness, or discovering non-obvious bundles.
questions.first_test: Restrict to top-N probe decks; build payoff tables for heuristic/counter_happy/threat_rush pilots; add an evolutionary constructor loop as a response oracle.
questions.risk: Simulator exploitation or overfitting to weak heuristic opponents.

questions.question: Does an agent learn a different keep/mulligan/bottom policy for 20 life vs 40 life, 40-card vs 60-card decks, and Force-heavy vs Jace-heavy construction?
questions.why_it_matters: Mulligan policy is part of the strategy bundle and can hide large construction advantages.
questions.first_test: Train or evolve a tiny policy over MULLIGAN_KEEP, MULLIGAN_TAKE, and MULLIGAN_BOTTOM(card); compare against keep_always/land_band baselines.
questions.risk: Reward noise from small game counts may favor overly aggressive mulligans.

questions.question: Can an agent learn to stall into max_decisions because draw-half scoring is beneficial in bad positions?
questions.why_it_matters: This is the cleanest MUC-5 reward-hack trap; it must be isolated before RL.
questions.first_test: Track truncation rate by strategy and use terminal-only reward for training unless truncation reward is explicitly enabled.
questions.risk: Long Jace mirrors can be legitimate; not every long game is a hack.

questions.question: How much stronger is an omniscient pilot than a public-observation pilot on the same deck?
questions.why_it_matters: This quantifies the value of hidden information and catches accidental leakage.
questions.first_test: Play trusted-state heuristics against public DecisionFrame equivalents; add a deliberate omniscient oracle only as an upper-bound benchmark.
questions.risk: Heuristic differences may reflect implementation style rather than information value.

questions.question: Once we have strategy-bundle payoff tables, does Alpha-Rank/PSRO-style population analysis tell a better story than single champion win rate?
questions.why_it_matters: MUC-5 may have rock-paper-scissors bundles: Force-heavy, Jace-heavy, Overlord-heavy, and deck-size gambits.
questions.first_test: Build a small empirical payoff matrix and compute simple stationary/population rankings before importing heavier solvers.
questions.risk: Sparse payoff estimates can make rankings unstable.

questions.question: Can a constructor exploit knowing 20 vs 40 life, and how much does robust unknown-life construction give up?
questions.why_it_matters: Life total changes Force cost, Overlord clocks, and Jace/decking pressure.
questions.first_test: Compare known_20, known_40, and unknown_robust shortlists across the same pilot population.
questions.risk: 40 life may mostly be a red herring if Jace/decking dominates.

questions.question: Can every surprising result be replayed exactly from an archived trace?
questions.why_it_matters: Without replay, strange learned behavior is just noise; with replay, we can inspect it and play against it.
questions.first_test: Record JSONL traces with state fingerprints and require replay pass before promoting payoff data.
questions.risk: Future simulator revisions may intentionally invalidate old traces; manifests must record revision.

questions.question: Does sampling plausible opponent hands/libraries improve play enough to justify information-set search?
questions.why_it_matters: MUC-5 is small but hidden-information; search should reason over beliefs, not true state.
questions.first_test: Build a shallow rollout agent that samples hidden states consistent with public observations and scores legal actions by rollouts.
questions.risk: Belief sampling can be biased if decklists are unknown or construction priors are wrong.

questions.question: Are constructors being evaluated with information they would not have at registration time?
questions.why_it_matters: Known vs unknown life, open vs closed decklists, and opponent pool access are separate tournament contexts.
questions.first_test: Make ConstructionContext part of every strategy-bundle metadata row and reject unlabeled rows.
questions.risk: Convenience scripts may accidentally mix contexts.

questions.question: Can a tiny masked neural policy beat heuristic pilots without seeing hidden state?
questions.why_it_matters: This is the first true ML pilot milestone after simulator confidence.
questions.first_test: Behavior-clone heuristic games or train REINFORCE/PPO-style on public DecisionFrames using action masks.
questions.risk: Sparse terminal rewards and slow CPU-only rollouts can make naive RL look worse than it is.
